questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Improper Integral Using a Substitution
questions.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u=\sqrt{x}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,⟹\,2\text{d}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=\sqrt{x}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{3}^{-\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{3}^{-u}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{3}^{-\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{3}^{-u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}{3}^{-u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{{3}^{-u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[{3}^{-u}]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\frac{1}{{3}^{a}}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\frac{1}{{3}^{x}},$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{{3}^{x}}=\infty $

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{3}^{x}}=0$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067475/assets/ff41c6fa5858f45e76a4d4fec0f0a8080300b69fcb632df60141d93c66f3cdd9.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{3}^{-\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\frac{1}{{3}^{a}}-1) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot (0-1) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{2}{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{2}{3}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{3}^{x}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }({3}^{2}-{3}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{3}^{a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={3}^{x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{3}^{x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{3}^{x}=\infty $

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Improper Integral Using a Substitution
questions.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u={x}^{3}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{3}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{5}^{u}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}{5}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{5}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}]}_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[{5}^{u}]_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(1-{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall the end behavior of the function $y={5}^{a},$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a}=0$

- ${lim}_{a\to \infty }{5}^{a}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067475/assets/c0c7699b036ebd8779cd6c3d3143cdcca6312834ee731e144e38488124164f43.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.\end{aligned}
$$
